title: kijönnek egymással: How Well People Get Along

sections.title: Putting kijön and egymás together
sections.content: You already know kijön valakivel ("to get along with someone"). Now that you have egymással, you can describe how well two or more people get along without naming either one twice: instead of Anna jól kijön Péterrel, és Péter jól kijön Annával, you can just say Anna és Péter jól kijönnek egymással. The same pattern works for megért ("to understand") with the accusative form egymást: megértik egymást, "they understand each other."

sections.title: Degrees of getting along
rows: they get along well with each other
they get along with difficulty / it's hard for them to get along
they get along badly with each other

items.spanish: A testvérem és én nagyon jól kijövünk egymással.
items.english: My sibling and I get along very well with each other.

items.spanish: Eleinte nehezen jöttünk ki egymással, de most már megértjük egymást.
items.english: At first we got along with difficulty, but now we understand each other.

items.spanish: Furcsa, milyen jól megértjük egymást, pedig nagyon különbözőek vagyunk.
items.english: It's strange how well we understand each other, even though we're very different.

sections.content: kijön is one of the ik-verbs whose plural forms drop the -ik: kijönnek (they get along), not kijönnek-ik. When you conjugate it for we/you-plural, remember the subject is now plural even if only egymással (singular in form) follows: (mi) jól kijövünk egymással, not kijövök.
